clue.text: Delivery man who may darken your doorway tonight

definitions.text: Delivery man who may darken your doorway tonight

parts.words: Delivery man who may darken your doorway tonight
parts.note: in Scottish custom the first visitor over the threshold after midnight on New Year's Eve brings gifts such as coal, so he delivers luck

explanation.surface: A sinister courier might be lurking at your door after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland and northern England the first person to cross the threshold after midnight at New Year traditionally brings coal, bread or whisky; a tall dark man is thought luckiest, hence 'darken your doorway'.
explanation.definitionFit: The custom's first New Year guest carries gifts, so he is literally a bringer of goods at that hour.

clue.text: Relief turns up in leading democracy

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up makes the letters read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: aid is relief, help for those in need

explanation.surface: Humanitarian help arrives in a nation that leads the democratic world.
explanation.definitionFit: With well over a billion citizens, the South Asian republic is often called the world's largest democracy.

clue.text: Man in charge of course, photographer needs another snooze

indicators.note: needs another says one nap is swapped for a different word with the same sense

parts.note: a snapper is slang for a photographer
a kip is a snooze, British slang for sleep

explanation.surface: A cameraman, of course, must have one more doze.
explanation.walkthrough: The NAP in SNAPPER is replaced by KIP, another word for a snooze. 'of course' reads as a shrug but belongs to the definition: a ship's captain directs its course.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's captain sets the vessel's heading, so he is the person commanding its route.

clue.text: Around Leamington Spa's outskirts, jolly 1950s youth showed off

indicators.note: around says the word for jolly goes round the outer letters

parts.note: a jolly is a fun outing, so fun

indicators.note: a town's outskirts are its edges, so only the outermost letters of the name are used

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress

explanation.surface: On the edge of a Warwickshire spa town, a cheery young rocker from the fifties paraded about.
explanation.walkthrough: The outskirts of Leamington Spa are its first and last letters, L and A. Teddy boys were a 1950s British youth subculture.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt something is to display it ostentatiously, so this past tense means paraded or displayed proudly.

clue.text: Nameless theatrical awards for items used in play?

indicators.note: nameless means without the letter N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: the Tonys are the American awards for Broadway theatre

explanation.surface: Unnamed stage prizes are given for props used in a production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' suggests the theatre, but here it is children at play.
explanation.definitionFit: Playthings are objects children use for amusement in games, so they are things used in play.

clue.text: Stimulate anew to download another 26?

definitions.meaning: to reawaken or arouse interest or feeling again
fanciful: to put another electronic book on one's Kindle reader once more

explanation.surface: Revive interest by fetching yet another digital book.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as RE-KINDLE: Kindle is Amazon's e-reader, and 26 across is EBOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse something again is to relight it, as a dying fire or a faded enthusiasm is revived.

clue.text: First of all, I'm not intending to idle about like last year. That's to begin with…

indicators.note: read literally, the first of all the following words, so their opening letters are taken

explanation.surface: A New Year's resolution: no more lazing about as I did last year, for a start.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean at the outset or in the first place, so they are synonyms for a starting point.

clue.text: Gum evidently endlessly chewed — there's an admission

indicators.note: chewed means mashed up, so the letters are rearranged
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone has plainly been chewing gum and owns up to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of EVIDENTLY; 'chewed' rearranges GUM with EVIDENTL.
explanation.definitionFit: Disclosing a secret is a revelation or confession, so it amounts to admitting something.

clue.text: World-weariness that is holding a French knight back

indicators.note: back tells us the whole assembled string is read in the reverse direction
holding says the abbreviation for that is grips the other pieces inside it

parts.note: IE (id est) is the abbreviation for that is
UN is the French word for a
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Someone tired of life clutches a French cavalier to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' looks like a mere link phrase but supplies the abbreviation i.e.; 'back' turns the assembled IUNNE round.
explanation.definitionFit: Boredom and listless weariness with everything is exactly this borrowed French word's meaning.

clue.text: In our time, military is deployed after one's left naval department

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters following the era abbreviation

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, marks dates in the present era, our time

indicators.note: troops being deployed are spread into new positions, so the letters are rearranged
left here means departed, so the letter for one is taken out

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is is

explanation.surface: A report on modern armed forces being sent out once a single person has quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' takes I from MILITARY, leaving MLITARY, which 'is deployed' rearranges into MIRALTY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Admiralty was the British government office that ran the Royal Navy until 1964.

clue.text: Quiet resort hit by rumour of zoo animal from China

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means sort again, so the letters are rearranged
a rumour is something heard spoken, so the letters entered match how the word sounds

parts.note: the word zoo, said, gives the sound spelt ZU

explanation.surface: A peaceful holiday spot is shaken by gossip about an escaped zoo creature from China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' rearranges HIT into IHT; 'rumour of' turns ZOO into its sound, ZU.
explanation.definitionFit: This small long-haired toy dog breed was developed in China, its name meaning lion dog.

clue.text: Why nary a peep exchanged in timely greeting?

indicators.note: exchanged means swapped around, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: Someone wonders why nobody uttered a sound when greetings were swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Said at midnight on 31 December, this salutation is perfectly timed to the calendar's turn.

clue.text: Flawed heroes sully games manual

indicators.note: flawed means faulty or broken, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: Imperfect champions besmirch the sporting contests.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmond Hoyle wrote eighteenth-century rulebooks on whist and other card games, so his name heads a handbook of game regulations.

clue.text: Fighting soldiers' rations?

definitions.meaning: fanciful: fare, meaning food, eaten in war

explanation.surface: Troops in combat are fed their provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: Military conflict waged between nations is armed combat, which is what fighting means here.

clue.text: Cast laud Spooner's chanted lyric in topical song

indicators.note: cast means shaped anew, as metal is cast, so the letters are rearranged
Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of two words trade places

parts.note: chanted means sang
a lyric is a line of a song

explanation.surface: Actors praise a lyric that has been sung in a song of the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' rearranges LAUD; swapping the first sounds of SANG LINE gives LANG SINE, spelt SYNE as in the Scots song. 'Topical' because it is sung at New Year, this puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns's Scots song is traditionally sung at midnight on New Year's Eve, so it fits the season's theme.

clue.text: See 12
Mutton dressed as lamb might appear in this majority

definitions.text: Mutton dressed as lamb might appear in this
definitions.meaning: fanciful: a grown sheep in disguise is an adult wearing a hood
the age of majority, when one is legally grown up

explanation.surface: An older person dressed too young might be seen like this by most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mutton dressed as lamb' is a British phrase for an older woman dressed too young; here it is read literally as a grown sheep in a hood.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching one's majority means attaining full legal age, the state of being grown up.

clue.text: Journalist provided with cool, complex organisation

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist
if means provided, as in on condition that
ice means to cool or chill

explanation.surface: A reporter, given a chilled reception, faces a complicated bureaucracy.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively the word means an elaborate structure of ideas or institutions, a complex system built up.

clue.text: Pinpoints signs of jewellery?

definitions.meaning: identifies or sets aside for a particular purpose
fanciful: marks on the ears left by earrings

explanation.surface: Someone spots the telltale traces of stolen gems.
explanation.definitionFit: To designate something for a purpose is to single it out, just as a pinpointed target is singled out.

clue.text: Rusty saw perhaps that's dropped by tree

definitions.meaning: a saw is a saying; an old, overused joke or saying is an example
a nut that falls from its tree in autumn

explanation.surface: A rusty saw, maybe, is something a tree lets fall.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: 'saw' is an old saying, not the tool, and an old chestnut is a stale joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a reddish-brown shade, a hackneyed tale, and the glossy nut of a familiar tree.

clue.text: See 14
Sea cub master knocked back bottles … a hangover in waiting?

indicators.note: knocked back says the hidden letters are read backwards
bottles means holds inside, so the answer sits within these clue words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A scout leader at sea gulps down drink, storing up a headache for tomorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'bottles' in the definition, but it is the indicator: 'Sea cub master' bottles the letters, and 'knocked back' reverses them. 'knocked back' also suggests drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian anise liqueur, drunk to excess it promises a sore head the next morning.

clue.text: Lustier dancing — Romeo gets closer

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so these are rearranged

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A randier dance where the romantic lead moves in tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closer' looks like nearness but means more oppressive, as close weather is humid.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather described as close is muggy and airless, so more humid and stifling heat is the comparative.

clue.text: Me sporting tailored sateen? Kind of right

indicators.note: someone sporting clothing wears it, so the cloth goes around the word for me
tailored fabric is cut and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders aloud whether to wear a custom-made glossy fabric outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Me sporting' means I am wearing it, so the rearranged cloth, EASENT, is wrapped around the speaker; 'Kind of right' is a legal term, not approval.
explanation.definitionFit: In law this is a right of way or use over another person's land, one particular type of legal entitlement.

clue.text: What's near end of 31st?

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: end of picks out the final character of the next word

explanation.surface: A riddle asks what comes as December's last day draws to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue is the definition too: the dark hours close the 31st, the eve of New Year.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark hours at the close of 31 December are when New Year's Eve is celebrated, ending the day.

clue.text: International alliance judged and ignored

parts.note: UN is the United Nations, an alliance of nations
a court that has heard a case has tried and judged it

explanation.surface: A world body has ruled on a matter and then disregarded it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea that goes unlistened to is passed over and disregarded, as with protests falling on deaf ears.

clue.text: Pet, we hear, is shy animal

indicators.note: we hear says the letters entered match the sound of the word

parts.note: dear and pet are both terms of endearment

explanation.surface: Apparently a household pet is a timid creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland grazer that bolts at the slightest disturbance is a classic timid creature.

clue.text: Big-hearted punters try wild celebration somewhere in Scotland

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Generous gamblers attempt a raucous party north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scottish capital's Hogmanay celebration is a huge open-air New Year's Eve gathering on its central streets.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the famous outdoor festivity held in the Scottish capital each Hogmanay, so a Scottish celebration.

clue.text: Honour reflected by fine online publication

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the other way round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A decoration is mirrored by a penalty in some digital publication.
explanation.definitionFit: A digital book read on screen or downloaded from the internet is a publication delivered online.

clue.text: See 25
